requiredFindings.title: Apply production-include confinement to integration-test files too
requiredFindings.finding: The revised include analysis rejects mixed test/production inclusions of src files such as installation_routing_tests.rs, but exempts every path containing /tests/ before examining its incoming edges. whole_test initializes these files to True and the fixed-point loop skips them forever. Thus a production include edge to crates/host/tests/admission_tests.rs leaves rustc_path (RUSTC), nested_cargo (CARGO) and the X8 helpers classified test-only, even while their existing item-level Clippy allowances remain. Their call and allowance sets do not change, so the pin cannot reject this production reachability. This contradicts the stated rule that one production-reachable inclusion makes a file production. The new negative control exercises a src/custody target, not this still-exempt target class.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Treat integration-test entry-point status as a test root, not an unconditional exemption from production reachability. Reject production-reachable include edges into those files and propagate that status through their includes; retain ordinary test-target classification when no production inclusion exists. Add a negative control introducing a real production include of an allowed tests/ file while preserving its integration-test role, and require the existing exception pin to reject it. Keep the successful src-file mixed-include and comment/literal controls.
evidence: whole_test = {rel: '/tests/' in rel for rel in codes}
if whole_test[rel]: continue prevents checking incoming production edges for these targets
The accepted r5 list requires all non-Git exceptions to remain test-only, including the host integration-test helpers
